facts.text: Swartswood Lake, a natural glacial lake formed over 10,000 years ago, sits at 525 ft elevation and stretches three miles along the ridge and valley region.
The community’s name honors Anthony Swartwout, a British militia soldier whose 1756 death and capture of his children by Lenape warriors delayed settlement for decades.
In 1824, Jonathan Oliver built a sawmill, tannery, and worker housing, renaming the area “New Paterson” before it became Swartswood in 1852.
Swartswood once thrived as a summer resort, drawing New Yorkers to its lake, hotels, and the 1938 North Shore House for boating and recreation.
Today the park offers year‑round activities, including 73 camping sites, hiking on the Duck Pond Trail, and winter ice fishing on the lake’s 519 acres.
Only electric motors are allowed on Swartswood Lake, so visitors enjoy peaceful sailboats, canoes, and kayaks instead of jet skis.
